Hydrogen ions are formed when glycolysis is being used as a major means of resynthesising ATP, as your team note says. In that case, lactate and H⁺ build up during high-intensity anaerobic work, and the H⁺ lowers muscle pH. My earlier answer, about acids donating protons in water, is true as general chemistry, but it doesn't fit this question's likely exercise-physiology context.

CONFIDENCE: 80
